topic: Akainu used a pirate's grudge against Roger to turn him against Whitebeard, weaponizing lineage itself
title: Akainu Weaponized A 20-Year Grudge
description: Akainu knew he couldn't beat Whitebeard alone, so he did something colder: he found a captain who lost his crew to Roger years earlier and convinced him Whitebeard was using him. One lie, one grudge, and Whitebeard's own family attacked him. Here's the manipulation most power-scaling videos skip.
comment: Does Akainu's manipulation of Squard prove he was never hunting raw strength at all?

lines.text: Squard lost his entire crew to Gol D. Roger years before Marineford even happened.

shot.fallback: grieving pirate captain alone at sea

lines.text: Whitebeard took him in afterward, raised him like one of his own sons in chapter 561.

shot.fallback: old emperor welcoming a broken pirate

lines.text: That's two decades of loyalty, one pirate owing everything to another.

shot.fallback: devoted pirate serving an old emperor

lines.text: Then Akainu walks up to Squard and tells him a lie: Whitebeard is abandoning the crew just to save Ace.
That lie is built specifically on a grudge Squard holds against Roger's lineage, not Whitebeard's actions.
Squard turns on the man who took him in, drives a blade straight through Whitebeard's body.

shot.fallback: pirate captain striking an old emperor

lines.text: Not because Whitebeard did anything wrong. Because a lie turned a lineage grudge into a weapon.
That's patience. That's playing for a longer game than one battle...

shot.fallback: admiral playing a slow careful game

self_check.hook: line 1 sets Squard's history (lost crew to Roger), line 2 adds stakes (Whitebeard raised him), line 4 states the claim (Akainu weaponized this via a lie)
self_check.loop: last line ('That's patience... a longer game') echoes the long's theme that Akainu played strategy, not raw power — loops back to the setup without repeating opening words
